## Method

**Certificates used.** Exact rational arithmetic is used for the leading Laurent coefficients, and the verifier compares coefficients as exact fractions [C-modular-R6d-RT2]. High-precision numerical evaluation at 32 digits is used for residuals [C-modell]. Singular values of a normalised value matrix are used for completeness [C-modular-R1]. None of the claims used here relies on symbolic positivity proofs or interval arithmetic.

**Trusted base.** The trusted base is the verifier's own evaluation of $E(s)$ and $C(a,b,c)$ at 32 digits at points it chooses itself [C-modell]. Relations proposed by a search are not trusted. Each one is re-checked as follows.

1. *Exact leading Laurent coefficient.* The verifier computes exactly the leading coefficient $y^w$ of the Laurent expansion of the proposed combination and requires it to vanish [C-modular-R6a][C-modular-R4a]. The claim record does not define the expansion variable $y$ further. This check is a necessary condition. Because it is exact, it does not depend on the finite-difference step, including for the Laplace equations [C-modular-R4a].
2. *Numerical residual.* The relation is evaluated at the 4 verifier points. The maximal relative residual must be below 1e-24 for linear relations and below 1e-14 for Laplace equations, where $L$ is a finite-difference Laplacian [C-modell].
3. *Completeness.* A normalised value matrix, with columns the functions and rows evaluation points, is decomposed by singular values, using seed 4712 [C-modular-R1]. The seed differs from the seed 4711 of the 4 verifier points, which suggests that it fixes the evaluation points of this matrix. The record does not state this. The matrices have 6, 7, 9 and 12 rows for 3, 4, 6 and 9 columns, so they have three more rows than columns in each case [C-modular-R1]. The record does not state how the number of rows is chosen. The dimension is the number of singular values below 1e-24, and a gap to the remaining values above 1e-8 is required [C-modular-R1].

**Numerical candidates.** Everything about $C(a,b,c)$ is a numerical observation. Exact leading coefficients are necessary conditions, not proofs. Completeness rests on a numerical singular-value gap at the tested points [C-modular-R1].

::: remark [Status of the computer-assisted parts]
No theorem about modular graph functions is claimed. The exact part of the trusted base is rational arithmetic for leading coefficients, and the numerical part is 32-digit evaluation by the verifier [C-modell][C-modular-R6d-RT2]. A third party re-runs everything with the commands of the Declarations [C-verfuegbarkeit].
:::

The results were produced by an automated, verifier-gated laboratory. Every statement was accepted only after code-based verification, and counter-hypotheses were tested adversarially [C-methode][C-redteam].

## Discussion, limitations and open questions

**Status.** All $C(a,b,c)$ statements rest on 32-digit evaluations and singular-value gaps [C-modell][C-modular-R1]. This is numerical evidence, not proof. Dimension 1 at each weight is a statement about the tested function sets only, which contain no products of Eisenstein series or zeta values [C-modular-R1d][C-modular-R6e-RT1]. The record contains no predicted dimensions from arXiv:2004.05156, so we make no quantitative comparison [C-modular-R1d]. Observations 1 to 3 and 5 to 7 reproduce or overlap known results, and the weight-9 identity has inconclusive novelty status [C-modular-R1c][C-modular-R4a][C-modular-R6a]. The weight-11 computation is still running, and all results are preliminary.

**Red-team record.** Of 25 adversarial counter-checks, 2 passed, 22 did not pass, and 1 was not executable [C-redteam]. A counter-check is built to succeed only if the claim is false, so "did not pass" supports the claim. The passed checks were consistency checks that do not contradict the statement [C-redteam][C-modular-R1c-RT1].

**Open questions.**

(i) Is the relation at each weight provable, for example by exact reduction of the lattice sums?

(ii) Does the generating-series counting of arXiv:2004.05156 reproduce the relation-space dimensions found here, in particular at weight 9 [C-modular-R1d]?

(iii) What is the relation space when products of Eisenstein series and zeta values are included in the function set at weights 5, 7 and 9 [C-modular-R6e-RT1]?

(iv) Can the weight-6 relation space be determined [C-neg1]?
